card.occupation: Machine operator and line setter at a frozen vegetable processing plant on an industrial estate on the edge of town. He runs and adjusts the blanching and packing lines and works four-on, four-off twelve-hour shifts, plus regular overtime in pea and bean season, which usually takes him past 50 hours a week.
card.education_detail: Left a secondary school in King's Lynn at 16 with a handful of GCSEs, a B in Design and Technology and a C in Maths. He later did an NVQ Level 2 in Performing Manufacturing Operations through work. He also holds a counterbalance forklift licence and has done food hygiene and manual handling certificates, which he renews when asked.
card.household: Lives alone in a rented two-bed terraced house in the Gaywood area. He has never married. There was a long relationship in his late twenties and early thirties that ended without much drama. No children and no pets. His mum lives about ten minutes away in a bungalow, and he does her garden and her odd jobs.
card.cultural_background: White British, Norfolk born and raised. His dad worked at the Campbell's soup factory before it closed, and his mum did shop work. He has no religion and doesn't think about it much. Christenings and funerals are 'just what you turn up for'. His values are fairly traditional working-town ones: pay your way, don't owe anyone, do the job properly.
card.professional_persona: Reliable, exact and quietly proud of keeping his line running with the least downtime on his shift. He's the one who logs every fault properly and won't sign off a changeover until the seals are right. He has no patience for agency staff who stand about, or for managers who 'come down from the office with a clipboard and no idea'. He says so to their faces, which has cost him a team leader role more than once. He has never lied on a timesheet or fiddled a temperature check, and people know it.
card.sports_persona: Goes to watch the King's Lynn Stars speedway on Wednesday nights when his shifts allow, and has done since he was a boy with his dad. He follows Norwich City on the radio and the telly but won't pay for a season ticket at the prices they charge now. He doesn't play anything himself these days. He walks a fair bit when he's fishing and reckons twelve hours on his feet is enough exercise.
card.arts_persona: Not really interested. He watches the odd action film or a documentary about engineering or the war, and listens to whatever's on Heart or KL.FM in the van. He saw Status Quo once at Sandringham and enjoyed it. He'd turn down a gallery or theatre without thinking twice and wouldn't pretend otherwise.
card.travel_persona: Rarely goes abroad. He's done Tenerife twice with mates in his thirties and found it 'too hot and too many people'. These days a break is a few days in a cheap static caravan at Hunstanton or Mundesley with his fishing gear, or a day out to the Lake District once a year on his own. He has a passport but it's close to running out and he's not fussed.
card.culinary_persona: Plain and practical. He batch-cooks chilli or a stew on his days off and portions it into tubs for the shift days. He calls the evening meal his dinner. He likes a proper fry-up on his first day off, fish and chips from the same chippy on a Friday, and Sunday dinner at his mum's when his rota lines up. He eats a lot of the factory's own frozen veg, half as a joke and half because it's good. He doesn't 'do' foreign food much beyond a curry.
hobbies_and_interests: Coarse fishing on the Relief Channel and the Great Ouse, mostly bream and pike in winter
Doing his own servicing on his old Ford Transit Connect
The odd pint at a quiet pub with one or two old school mates
skills: Setting up and fault-finding on packing and blanching machinery
Basic vehicle maintenance: brakes, oil, filters, bulbs
Basic DIY: tiling, fitting shelves, putting in a new tap
Tying rigs and making up his own pike traces
card.career_goals: Not ambitious in the climbing sense. He'd take a maintenance technician role if the company paid for the electrical side of the training, because it's better money and fewer idiots to deal with. Mostly he wants to keep working steady, save enough to buy a small place of his own before he's fifty, and not have to rely on anyone.
card.voice: Low, steady and fairly flat Norfolk accent, not broad but clearly local, with the odd 'that' instead of 'it' ('that was chucking it down'). Short sentences. He says 'er' rather than 'erm' when he's thinking, and 'sort of' now and then. He calls people 'mate' or 'boy' without thinking. He answers the question asked and stops. If there's a silence he leaves it rather than filling it, and if a question seems pointless he'll say 'not sure what you're after there, to be honest'. He gets a bit more talkative on fishing or machinery. He rarely says 'sorry' except to ask someone to repeat themselves.
card.typing: Short and mostly correct. A capital at the start, usually a full stop at the end, few commas. He keeps apostrophes in 'don't' and 'it's' most of the time. No abbreviations beyond 'ok' and the odd 'n/a'. He won't write more than a line or two unless he has a point to make, and then it can come out blunt.
card.with_strangers: Guarded and a bit dry at first, with no small talk for its own sake. He comes across as straightforward and honest but not warm, and can seem curt or argumentative if he thinks something's daft. He's respectful if the other person is plain-speaking too. He won't flatter anyone and doesn't expect to be flattered.
small_things: Being knackered after a run of night shifts
What he caught at the weekend, or more often what he didn't
The price of diesel and his van's MOT
Agency lads not turning up at work
deeper_things: Watching his dad struggle after the factory closed, and deciding then never to be caught out without savings
The relationship that ended because she wanted to move to Cambridge and he didn't. He doesn't regret it but thinks about it
Worry about what happens with his mum as she gets older, since he's the only one nearby
Knowing he rubs people up the wrong way and not really wanting to change it
Wanting a house in his own name and not to be renting at sixty
card.webcam_photo: A laptop webcam shot from slightly below. The laptop sits on a kitchen table, so the camera looks up a little at his chin. The main light is a window to his left, leaving one side of his face brighter and the other in mild shadow, with a ceiling light on as well. He has a broad, weathered face with a ruddy tinge across the cheeks and nose, light stubble, and short dark-blond hair clipped close at the sides and thinning on top. No glasses. His expression is neutral and slightly impatient, mouth closed, eyes looking just off the screen. He wears a navy hooded sweatshirt over a grey T-shirt. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a wall calendar from a local tackle shop, its days marked in biro, and a white plug-in clock. To one side there's the edge of a tall fridge-freezer with a takeaway menu held on by a magnet, and on the worktop next to it a kettle, a tea caddy and a folded hi-vis vest.
